risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The corn starch industry is witnessing increased capacity expansion by existing players, entry of new players and growing availability of substitute materials; higher domestic maize prices vs. steady international maize prices is pressuring the Company's pricing in export markets and may impact export market share.
- Maize, an agricultural product, is highly vulnerable to climate change — droughts, floods, heatwaves, pests and diseases can disrupt corn production, causing shortages and higher production costs, with power costs also affected by input-cost dynamics.
- Increasing regulation and changing government policy on sustainability and climate change (including India's NDC targets) could result in fines, legal action and reputational damage if the Company fails to comply.
- As a company based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, the Company is exposed to acute physical risks such as floods, droughts, storms, fires and heavy rains that could affect manufacturing facilities, inventory, supply chain and delivery.
- Exposure to compliance with government regulations, intellectual property disputes and contractual obligations; failure to comply with legal requirements or contractual obligations could significantly impact business, reputation and financial performance.
- Failure to keep pace with evolving technology in the corn wet-milling industry could impact competitiveness in efficiency, waste reduction and product quality.
- Growing customer demand for sustainable sourcing and production processes is a market risk; customers increasingly evaluate suppliers on sustainability and environment parameters in addition to price and quality.
